summary: DevOps team cannot assume 'service-deployer' role after Okta group-prefix normalization; temporary elevation requested
description:
Issue summary: Members of the DevOps team report they can no longer assume the internal 'service-deployer' RBAC role in the Deploy Console after an Okta group-attribute prefix normalization rollout last night. Impact: ~6 engineers (devops, platform) cannot perform deploys or create canary releases; blocked on critical patch deploy. No service-side errors are thrown when attempting 'assume-role' — the console returns 403 and the frontend shows 'insufficient permissions'.

Environment: Production, Deploy Console (deploy-console.redwood.com), auth mediated via Okta SAML + JIT SCIM group sync. Issue appeared after a mass SCIM normalization job (okta-sync v2.3.0) completed at 2026-03-09 22:17 UTC.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Log in as a DevOps user (e.g., a.patel@redwood.example) via Okta SSO.
2) Open Deploy Console -> Projects -> pick any project -> click 'New Release' -> choose 'Create Canary'.
3) Attempt to 'Assume role' service-deployer from the role dropdown.
4) Observe the failure: 403 UI message and no network call to role-assignment microservice appears in browser network tab.

Observed behavior: Users in Okta group 'devops-service-deployers' are displayed in Okta and SCIM reports as members, but our RBAC mapping service is returning "no matching role mapping" for those subjects. The deploy-console logs show auth assertion received with attribute "groups": ["team/devops-service-deployers"] (note the new 'team/' prefix). Older role mapping rules expected the bare group name without the prefix.

Expected behavior: JIT provisioning or RBAC mapping should tolerate canonicalization/prefix changes or we should have a migration that updates role-mapping rules. Users should be able to assume the 'service-deployer' role without manual intervention.

Temporary workaround requested: Grant temporary 'service-deployer' role directly in the RBAC service for the listed affected users or add an allowlist exemption for the 'team/' prefixed groups until permanent mapping is fixed. Also request an emergency runbook entry describing detection and mitigation.

Attachments / references: Okta SCIM audit job id: scim-job-20260309-2217; rollout PR: github.com/redwood-inference/okta-sync/pull/412; deployed image: okta-sync:2.3.0; related incident channel: #support-identity.

Navigate to Deploy Console -> Projects -> New Release -> Create Canary
Attempt to 'Assume role' service-deployer from the role dropdown
Observe 403 'insufficient permissions' in UI and no role-assignment call from frontend

2026-03-10T09:03:12Z WARN rbac-mapper: no mapping found for group 'team/devops-service-deployers' when resolving roles for user 'a.patel@redwood.example'
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:15 - Identity: Confirmed normalization job ran and prefixed groups with 'team/' per new standardization rules
03/10 09:22 - RBAC: Current mapping table contains entries for 'devops-service-deployers' (no prefix). Mapper matches exact string; no fallback configured
03/10 09:40 - Temporary test: added a mapping alias for 'team/devops-service-deployers' in rbac-mapper dev cluster; test user able to assume role successfully in staging
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10 09:05): We're blocked on a security patch rollout — can we get emergency escalation? I can provide affected usernames.
Morgan Reyes (2026-03-10 09:18): Assigned. Initial hypothesis: SCIM normalization added a namespace prefix. Asking Identity team for confirmation and quick mitigation options.

Jordan Kim - Identity (2026-03-10 09:25): Confirmed scim-job-20260309-2217 applied 'team/' prefix. This was intended for future-onboarding consistency; we missed adding backward-compatible aliases. Preparing a hotfix to write alias entries to the mapping cache.

SRE Lead - Priya Menon (2026-03-10 09:40): Recommend temporary role grant via RBAC admin API as fastest path. If we do this, include expiry and audit log entry. Preparing a script to grant to 6 users.

Morgan Reyes (2026-03-10 10:05): Executed temporary grants for the 6 affected identities (audit id: rbac-tempgrant-20260310-1005). Verified two users can create canaries now. Leaving open until permanent fix deployed.

Jordan Kim - Identity (2026-03-12 16:50): Hotfix PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-mapper/pull/129 added prefix-tolerant matching and config flag to enable legacy aliases. Deploying to prod tonight at 02:00 UTC. Will update when live.

Morgan Reyes (2026-03-12 21:30): Prod change deployed. Verified mapping now resolves both prefixed and non-prefixed group names. Removing temporary grants as part of rollback plan. Closing after 24h stable verification.
resolution_notes: Temporary grants applied for affected users (rbac-tempgrant-20260310-1005). Permanent fix: rbac-mapper updated to support prefix-tolerant matching and legacy aliases (PR 129). Prod deployed 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. Monitored 24h: no further failures. Temporary grants revoked 2026-03-12 21:45 UTC. Follow-up: Identity to include compatibility step when changing SCIM canonicalization rules and add unit test to prevent regression.
